title.zh: 三大保健穴位：合谷、足三里、三阴交
title.en: Three Essential Health Acupoints: Hegu, Zusanli, Sanyinjiao

description.zh: 详解合谷、足三里、三阴交三大保健穴位的定位、功效和按摩方法，日常保健必备
description.en: Detailed guide to three essential health acupoints - location, benefits, and massage techniques for daily wellness

zh.text: 在中医针灸经络体系中，有三个穴位被历代医家誉为"保健三穴"——合谷、足三里和三阴交。这三个穴位各踞一方、各有所长，覆盖了人体从头部到腹部再到下肢的广泛调理范围。《针灸甲乙经》中对这三个穴位的定位和主治已有明确记载，历经千年临床验证，至今仍是中医养生中应用最广、效果最确切的穴位组合。
合谷穴属于手阳明大肠经，位于手背第一、二掌骨之间，约在第二掌骨桡侧中点处。简便取穴法：将拇指和食指并拢，手背肌肉隆起的最高点即是。《针灸甲乙经》记载："合谷，在手大指次指间。"此穴是四总穴之一，有"面口合谷收"之说，意思是头面部的各种疾病都可以通过合谷穴来调理。

合谷穴的核心功效在于止痛和疏风解表。临床中无论是风寒感冒引起的头痛身痛，还是风热上攻导致的咽喉肿痛、牙痛，合谷都有确切的缓解效果。从中医机理来看，大肠经与肺经相表里，肺主皮毛，故而刺激合谷可以"开腠理、驱外邪"。对于现代人常见的偏头痛、牙龈炎、过敏性鼻炎，我都常提醒患者配合按压合谷。此外合谷还有安神镇静的作用，对于焦虑紧张引起的失眠也有帮助。按摩手法：用对侧拇指指腹垂直按压，力度以产生明显的酸胀感为宜，每次3至5分钟，每日2至3次。需要特别提醒的是，孕妇慎用合谷穴，因本穴有较强的行气活血作用，不当刺激可能影响妊娠。
足三里是足阳明胃经的合穴，位于小腿外侧，犊鼻穴下3寸，距胫骨前缘外一横指处。简便取穴：正坐屈膝，以手掌盖住膝盖，中指尖所指处向外一横指即是。此穴在中医界的地位极高，民间素有"若要安，三里常不干"的古谚，意指若要身体健康平安，应当经常艾灸足三里，使局部保持温热。

足三里是中医公认的"强壮要穴"。它的核心功效可以概括为两大方面：第一，健脾和胃、调理中焦。凡是胃痛、腹胀、消化不良、腹泻或便秘等胃肠问题，足三里都是首选穴位。《灵枢·五邪》记载："邪在脾胃……皆调于三里。"第二，补中益气、强身健体。脾胃为后天之本、气血生化之源，足三里通过鼓舞脾胃之气，达到增强免疫力、延缓衰老的效果。在门诊中，对于体虚易感冒的儿童和免疫力下降的中老年人，我常建议他们每天按揉足三里，或隔姜灸此穴以培补元气。按摩手法：用拇指或中指按压，力度适中，每次5至10分钟，每日1至2次。艾灸效果更佳，每次15至20分钟，以局部皮肤温热红润为度。
三阴交是足太阴脾经的重要穴位，位于小腿内侧，内踝尖上3寸，胫骨内侧缘后方。简便取穴：以内踝尖为起点，向上四横指（同身寸3寸），胫骨后缘处。该穴之所以名为"三阴交"，是因为它是足太阴脾经、足厥阴肝经、足少阴肾经三条阴经的交会穴，一穴而通调肝、脾、肾三脏，在妇科疾病和内科杂病的调理中应用极广。

三阴交的核心功效包括调补肝肾、健脾利湿和安神助眠。在妇科方面，三阴交的地位几乎无可替代——月经不调、痛经、经前综合征、更年期综合征皆可调治。在临床中我发现，痛经患者在经前一周开始按揉三阴交，多数能显著减轻疼痛。此外，三阴交对于脾虚湿盛引起的水肿、小便不利也有良效。因脾主运化水湿，肝主疏泄条达，肾主气化水液，三穴共调则水湿自去。对于失眠多梦的患者，睡前按揉三阴交配合神门穴，常有出人意料的安神效果。按摩手法：用拇指按压，力度以有酸胀感为度，每次3至5分钟，每日1至2次。要注意的是，孕妇绝对禁用三阴交，因该穴可能引起子宫收缩，有流产风险。
三个穴位的搭配使用建议
在临床实践中，这三个穴位并非各自独立，而是可以根据体质和症状灵活搭配。比如气虚体质者，可重点使用足三里配合合谷，以补气固表；女性月经不调者，以三阴交为主、配合足三里，以调补气血；感冒初起时，以合谷为主、配合足三里，以疏风散寒。日常保健的话，每天早晚各花5分钟，依次按揉这三个穴位，坚持下来对提升整体健康水平大有裨益。按摩时需保持身心放松、呼吸自然。
温馨提示：穴位按摩是日常保健方法，不能替代医疗治疗。如有疾病症状，请及时就医。

en.text: In the TCM meridian and acupoint system, three acupoints have been celebrated by physicians throughout the ages as the 'Health Trio' — Hegu (LI4), Zusanli (ST36), and Sanyinjiao (SP6). Each occupies a distinct region of the body with unique therapeutic strengths, collectively covering a broad range of conditions from head to abdomen to lower limbs. The Zhenjiu Jiayi Jing (A-B Classic of Acupuncture and Moxibustion) clearly documented the locations and indications of these three points. After millennia of clinical validation, they remain the most widely used and reliably effective acupoint combination in TCM wellness practice.

Hegu belongs to the Hand Yangming Large Intestine meridian. It is located on the dorsum of the hand, between the first and second metacarpal bones, at the radial midpoint of the second metacarpal. A simple locating method: bring your thumb and index finger together; the highest point of the muscle bulge on the back of the hand is the point. The Zhenjiu Jiayi Jing records: "Hegu lies between the thumb and index finger." This point is one of the Four Master Points, known by the maxim "Face and mouth conditions seek Hegu" — meaning most head and facial disorders can be addressed through this point.

Hegu's core functions are pain relief and releasing the exterior to expel wind. In clinical practice, whether it is headache and body aches from wind-cold common cold, or sore throat and toothache from wind-heat attacking upward, Hegu provides reliable relief. From a TCM mechanism perspective, the Large Intestine meridian is internally-externally paired with the Lung meridian, and the Lung governs the skin and body hair — thus stimulating Hegu can "open the interstices and expel external pathogens." For modern complaints such as migraines, gingivitis, and allergic rhinitis, I routinely advise patients to press Hegu. It also calms the spirit, aiding those with anxiety-induced insomnia. Massage technique: press vertically with the thumb pad of the opposite hand until a distinct soreness is felt, 3-5 minutes per session, 2-3 times daily. Caution: pregnant women should use Hegu cautiously, as it strongly moves Qi and Blood and improper stimulation may affect pregnancy.

Zusanli is the He-Sea point of the Foot Yangming Stomach meridian, located on the outer lower leg, 3 cun below Dubi (ST35, lateral knee depression), one finger-width lateral to the anterior border of the tibia. Simple locating method: in a seated position with knee bent, place your palm over the kneecap; the point is one finger-width outward from where your middle finger tip reaches. This point holds an exceptionally high status in TCM. An ancient proverb says: "For peace and health, keep Zusanli moist" — meaning to maintain health, one should regularly apply moxibustion to Zusanli, keeping the area warm.

Zusanli is universally recognized as the primary acupoint for strengthening the body. Its core functions can be summarized in two aspects. First, it strengthens the Spleen and harmonizes the Stomach, regulating the middle burner. For all gastric issues — stomach pain, bloating, indigestion, diarrhea, or constipation — Zusanli is the point of first choice. The Lingshu states: "When pathogens lodge in the Spleen and Stomach... regulate them through Zusanli." Second, it tonifies middle Qi and strengthens the body. As the Spleen and Stomach are the acquired foundation and source of Qi and Blood production, Zusanli boosts Spleen-Stomach Qi to enhance immunity and delay aging. In clinic, for children prone to colds and middle-aged or elderly patients with declining immunity, I recommend daily massage of Zusanli or moxibustion over ginger slices to cultivate Yuan Qi. Massage technique: press with thumb or middle finger, moderate pressure, 5-10 minutes per session, 1-2 times daily. Moxibustion is even more effective — 15-20 minutes per session until the local skin becomes warm and slightly flushed.

Sanyinjiao is an important point of the Foot Taiyin Spleen meridian, located on the medial lower leg, 3 cun above the tip of the medial malleolus, posterior to the medial border of the tibia. Simple locating method: measure four finger-widths upward from the medial malleolus tip, behind the tibia. The name "Sanyinjiao" means "intersection of three Yin" — it is the meeting point of the Foot Taiyin Spleen, Foot Jueyin Liver, and Foot Shaoyin Kidney meridians. A single point that regulates three organs simultaneously, it is extensively used in gynecological disorders and various internal medicine conditions.

Sanyinjiao's core functions include tonifying the Liver and Kidney, strengthening the Spleen to resolve dampness, and calming the spirit to aid sleep. In gynecology, its status is nearly irreplaceable — it treats irregular menstruation, dysmenorrhea, premenstrual syndrome, and menopausal syndrome. In my clinical experience, patients with dysmenorrhea who begin pressing Sanyinjiao one week before menstruation experience significantly reduced pain. Additionally, Sanyinjiao is effective for edema and urinary difficulty caused by Spleen deficiency with dampness. Because the Spleen governs fluid transportation, the Liver governs free flow, and the Kidney governs fluid Qi transformation, regulating all three through this single point efficiently resolves dampness. For patients with insomnia and excessive dreaming, pressing Sanyinjiao before bed — combined with Shenmen (HT7) — often produces surprising calming effects. Massage technique: press with thumb until a comfortable soreness is felt, 3-5 minutes per session, 1-2 times daily. Important: Sanyinjiao is absolutely contraindicated during pregnancy, as it may stimulate uterine contractions and pose a risk of miscarriage.

In clinical practice, these three points are not used in isolation but can be flexibly combined based on constitution and symptoms. For Qi deficiency constitution, focus on Zusanli combined with Hegu to tonify Qi and secure the exterior. For menstrual irregularities, use Sanyinjiao as the primary point with Zusanli as a supplement to regulate Qi and nourish Blood. At the onset of a common cold, use Hegu as primary with Zusanli to release wind-cold. For daily wellness maintenance, spend about 5 minutes in the morning and evening pressing these three points in sequence. Consistent practice yields significant improvements in overall health. During massage, maintain physical and mental relaxation with natural breathing.
Note: Acupoint massage is for daily health maintenance and does not replace medical treatment. Seek medical care for disease symptoms.
